The chairman of the forum, Dr Peter Waziri, disclosed this during the formal inauguration of SKAD-F held at the Federal University of Applied Sciences, Kachia, over the weekend, where he identified the proposed library as the organisation’s first major developmental project.
Waziri said the facility would serve as a physical and digital repository of scholarly publications, research findings, historical records and cultural artefacts from the various ethnic communities of Southern Kaduna.
According to him, the project is designed to support researchers, students, academic institutions and members of the public, while ensuring that the region’s historical heritage is preserved for future generations.
He said the forum had already established an endowment fund to support the actualisation of the project.
Waziri appealed to the Kaduna State Government, traditional institutions, corporate organisations, development partners, philanthropists and well-meaning individuals to support the initiative.
“This is not merely a project for SKAD-F; it is an investment in the intellectual future, historical preservation and collective development of Southern Kaduna,” he said.
The chairman explained that the forum was established to harness the intellectual capacities and professional experiences of doctoral degree holders across academia, business, industry, politics and other sectors for the development of the region.
He said academic qualifications and professional accomplishments must translate into tangible benefits for society through community development, policy engagement, mentorship and practical solutions to societal challenges.
Waziri also highlighted the forum’s collaborations with the Kaduna State Government and the Southern Kaduna Association for Integrated Development (SKAID).
He said SKAD-F had partnered with SKAID on entrepreneurship training for young people in Kafanchan and Kaduna metropolis, while also mentoring beneficiaries of its scholarship scheme in tertiary institutions across the country.
The forum, he added, was committed to encouraging younger academics to pursue doctoral qualifications and contribute to research and knowledge production.
Waziri said the inauguration would also provide a platform for the forum to introduce its vision and aspirations to the wider public.
He stressed that SKAD-F was not in competition with existing groups in Southern Kaduna but intended to work with them towards the progress and development of the region.
